texts.jon.1.1: Y FUÉ palabra de Jehová á Jonás, hijo de Amittai, diciendo:
texts.jon.1.2: Levántate, y ve á Nínive, ciudad grande, y pregona contra ella; porque su maldad ha subido delante de mí.
texts.jon.1.3: Y Jonás se levantó para huir de la presencia de Jehová á Tarsis, y descendió á Joppe; y halló un navío que partía para Tarsis; y pagando su pasaje entró en él, para irse con ellos á Tarsis de delante de Jehová.
texts.jon.1.4: Mas Jehová hizo levantar un gran viento en la mar, é hízose una tan gran tempestad en la mar, que pensóse se rompería la nave.
texts.jon.1.5: Y los marineros tuvieron miedo, y cada uno llamaba á su dios: y echaron á la mar los enseres que había en la nave, para descargarla de ellos. Jonás empero se había bajado á los lados del buque, y se había echado á dormir.
texts.jon.1.6: Y el maestre de la nave se llegó á él, y le dijo: ¿Qué tienes, dormilón? Levántate, y clamá á tu Dios; quizá él tendrá compasión de nosotros, y no pereceremos.
texts.jon.1.7: Y dijeron cada uno á su compañero: Venid, y echemos suertes, para saber por quién nos ha venido este mal. Y echaron suertes, y la suerte cayó sobre Jonás.
texts.jon.1.8: Entonces le dijeron ellos: Decláranos ahora por qué nos ha venido este mal. ¿Qué oficio tienes, y de dónde vienes? ¿cuál es tu tierra, y de qué pueblo eres?
texts.jon.1.9: Y él les respondió: Hebreo soy, y temo á Jehová, Dios de los cielos, que hizo la mar y la tierra.
texts.jon.1.10: Y aquellos hombres temieron sobremanera, y dijéronle: ¿Por qué has hecho esto? Porque ellos entendieron que huía de delante de Jehová, porque se lo había declarado.
texts.jon.1.11: Y dijéronle: ¿Qué te haremos, para que la mar se nos quiete? porque la mar iba á más, y se embravecía.
texts.jon.1.12: El les respondió: Tomadme, y echadme á la mar, y la mar se os quietará: porque yo sé que por mí ha venido esta grande tempestad sobre vosotros.
texts.jon.1.13: Y aquellos hombres trabajaron por tornar la nave á tierra; mas no pudieron, porque la mar iba á más, y se embravecía sobre ellos.
texts.jon.1.14: Entonces clamaron á Jehová, y dijeron: Rogámoste ahora, Jehová, que no perezcamos nosotros por la vida de aqueste hombre, ni pongas sobre nosotros la sangre inocente: porque tú, Jehová, has hecho como has querido.
texts.jon.1.15: Y tomaron á Jonás, y echáronlo á la mar; y la mar se quietó de su furia.
texts.jon.1.16: Y temieron aquellos hombres á Jehová con gran temor; y ofrecieron sacrificio á Jehová, y prometieron votos.
texts.jon.1.17: MAS Jehová había prevenido un gran pez que tragase á Jonás: y estuvo Jonás en el vientre del pez tres días y tres noches.
texts.jon.2.1: Y oró Jonás desde el vientre del pez á Jehová su Dios.
texts.jon.2.2: Y dijo: Clamé de mi tribulación á Jehová, Y él me oyó; Del vientre del sepulcro clamé, Y mi voz oiste.
texts.jon.2.3: Echásteme en el profundo, en medio de los mares, Y rodeóme la corriente; Todas tus ondas y tus olas pasaron sobre mí.
texts.jon.2.4: Y yo dije: Echado soy de delante de tus ojos: Mas aun veré tu santo templo.
texts.jon.2.5: Las aguas me rodearon hasta el alma, Rodeóme el abismo; La ova se enredó á mi cabeza.
texts.jon.2.6: Descendí á las raíces de los montes; La tierra echó sus cerraduras sobre mí para siempre: Mas tú sacaste mi vida de la sepultura, oh Jehová Dios mío.
texts.jon.2.7: Cuando mi alma desfallecía en mí, acordéme de Jehová; Y mi oración entró hasta ti en tu santo templo.
texts.jon.2.8: Los que guardan las vanidades ilusorias, Su misericordia abandonan.
texts.jon.2.9: Yo empero con voz de alabanza te sacrificaré; Pagaré lo que prometí. La salvación pertenece á Jehová.
texts.jon.2.10: Y mandó Jehová al pez, y vomitó á Jonás en tierra.
texts.jon.3.1: Y FUÉ palabra de Jehová segunda vez á Jonás, diciendo:
texts.jon.3.2: Levántate, y ve á Nínive, aquella gran ciudad, y publica en ella el pregón que yo te diré.
texts.jon.3.3: Y levantóse Jonás, y fué á Nínive, conforme á la palabra de Jehová. Y era Nínive ciudad sobremanera grande, de tres días de camino.
texts.jon.3.4: Y comenzó Jonás á entrar por la ciudad, camino de un día, y pregonaba diciendo: De aquí á cuarenta días Nínive será destruida.
texts.jon.3.5: Y los hombres de Nínive creyeron á Dios, y pregonaron ayuno, y vistiéronse de sacos desde el mayor de ellos hasta el menor de ellos.
texts.jon.3.6: Y llegó el negocio hasta el rey de Nínive, y levantóse de su silla, y echó de sí su vestido, y cubrióse de saco, y se sentó sobre ceniza.
texts.jon.3.7: E hizo pregonar y anunciar en Nínive, por mandado del rey y de sus grandes, diciendo: Hombres y animales, bueyes y ovejas, no gusten cosa alguna, no se les dé alimento, ni beban agua:
texts.jon.3.8: Y que se cubran de saco los hombres y los animales, y clamen á Dios fuertemente: y conviértase cada uno de su mal camino, de la rapiña que está en sus manos.
texts.jon.3.9: ¿Quién sabe si se volverá y arrepentirá Dios, y se apartará del furor de su ira, y no pereceremos?
texts.jon.3.10: Y vió Dios lo que hicieron, que se convirtieron de su mal camino: y arrepintióse del mal que había dicho les había de hacer, y no lo hizo.
texts.jon.4.1: PERO Jonás se apesadumbró en extremo, y enojóse.
texts.jon.4.2: Y oró á Jehová, y dijo: Ahora, oh Jehová, ¿no es esto lo que yo decía estando aún en mi tierra? Por eso me precaví huyendo á Tarsis; porque sabía yo que tú eres Dios clemente y piadoso, tardo á enojarte, y de grande misericordia, y que te arrepientes del
texts.jon.4.3: Ahora pues, oh Jehová, ruégote que me mates; porque mejor me es la muerte que la vida.
texts.jon.4.4: Y Jehová le dijo: ¿Haces tú bien en enojarte tanto?
texts.jon.4.5: Y salióse Jonás de la ciudad, y asentó hacia el oriente de la ciudad, é hízose allí una choza, y se sentó debajo de ella á la sombra, hasta ver qué sería de la ciudad.
texts.jon.4.6: Y preparó Jehová Dios una calabacera, la cual creció sobre Jonás para que hiciese sombra sobre su cabeza, y le defendiese de su mal: y Jonás se alegró grandemente por la calabacera.
texts.jon.4.7: Mas Dios preparó un gusano al venir la mañana del día siguiente, el cual hirió á la calabacera, y secóse.
texts.jon.4.8: Y acaeció que al salir el sol, preparó Dios un recio viento solano; y el sol hirió á Jonás en la cabeza, y desmayábase, y se deseaba la muerte, diciendo: Mejor sería para mí la muerte que mi vida.
texts.jon.4.9: Entonces dijo Dios á Jonás: ¿Tanto te enojas por la calabacera? Y él respondió: Mucho me enojo, hasta la muerte.
texts.jon.4.10: Y dijo Jehová: Tuviste tú lástima de la calabacera, en la cual no trabajaste, ni tú la hiciste crecer; que en espacio de una noche nació, y en espacio de otra noche pereció:
texts.jon.4.11: ¿Y no tendré yo piedad de Nínive, aquella grande ciudad donde hay más de ciento y veinte mil personas que no conocen su mano derecha ni su mano izquierda, y muchos animales?

texts.jon.1.1: Now the word of Jehovah came unto Jonah the son of Amittai, saying,
texts.jon.1.2: Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me.
texts.jon.1.3: But Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of Jehovah; and he went down to Joppa, and found a ship going to Tarshish: so he paid the fare thereof, and went down into it, to go with them unto Tarshish from the presence of Jehovah.
texts.jon.1.4: But Jehovah sent out a great wind upon the sea, and there was a mighty tempest on the sea, so that the ship was like to be broken.
texts.jon.1.5: Then the mariners were afraid, and cried every man unto his god; and they cast forth the wares that were in the ship into the sea, to lighten it unto them. But Jonah was gone down into the innermost parts of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.
texts.jon.1.6: So the shipmaster came to him, and said unto him, What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we perish not.
texts.jon.1.7: And they said every one to his fellow, Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil is upon us. So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.
texts.jon.1.8: Then said they unto him, Tell us, we pray thee, for whose cause this evil is upon us; what is thine occupation? and whence comest thou? what is thy country? and of what people art thou?
texts.jon.1.9: And he said unto them, I am a Hebrew; and I fear Jehovah, the God of heaven, who hath made the sea and the dry land.
texts.jon.1.10: Then were the men exceedingly afraid, and said unto him, What is this that thou hast done? For the men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of Jehovah, because he had told them.
texts.jon.1.11: Then said they unto him, What shall we do unto thee, that the sea may be calm unto us? for the sea grew more and more tempestuous.
texts.jon.1.12: And he said unto them, Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you.
texts.jon.1.13: Nevertheless the men rowed hard to get them back to the land; but they could not: for the sea grew more and more tempestuous against them.
texts.jon.1.14: Wherefore they cried unto Jehovah, and said, We beseech thee, O Jehovah, we beseech thee, let us not perish for this man's life, and lay not upon us innocent blood; for thou, O Jehovah, hast done as it pleased thee.
texts.jon.1.15: So they took up Jonah, and cast him forth into the sea; and the sea ceased from its raging.
texts.jon.1.16: Then the men feared Jehovah exceedingly; and they offered a sacrifice unto Jehovah, and made vows.
texts.jon.1.17: And Jehovah prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah; and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
texts.jon.2.1: Then Jonah prayed unto Jehovah his God out of the fish's belly.
texts.jon.2.2: And he said, I called by reason of mine affliction unto Jehovah, And he answered me; Out of the belly of Sheol cried I, [And] thou heardest my voice.
texts.jon.2.3: For thou didst cast me into the depth, in the heart of the seas, And the flood was round about me; All thy waves and thy billows passed over me.
texts.jon.2.4: And I said, I am cast out from before thine eyes; Yet I will look again toward thy holy temple.
texts.jon.2.5: The waters compassed me about, even to the soul; The deep was round about me; The weeds were wrapped about my head.
texts.jon.2.6: I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; The earth with its bars [closed] upon me for ever: Yet hast thou brought up my life from the pit, O Jehovah my God.
texts.jon.2.7: When my soul fainted within me, I remembered Jehovah; And my prayer came in unto thee, into thy holy temple.
texts.jon.2.8: They that regard lying vanities Forsake their own mercy.
texts.jon.2.9: But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that which I have vowed. Salvation is of Jehovah.
texts.jon.2.10: And Jehovah spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.
texts.jon.3.1: And the word of Jehovah came unto Jonah the second time, saying,
texts.jon.3.2: Arise, go unto Nineveh, that great city, and preach unto it the preaching that I bid thee.
texts.jon.3.3: So Jonah arose, and went unto Nineveh, according to the word of Jehovah. Now Nineveh was an exceeding great city, of three days' journey.
texts.jon.3.4: And Jonah began to enter into the city a day's journey, and he cried, and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.
texts.jon.3.5: And the people of Nineveh believed God; and they proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.
texts.jon.3.6: And the tidings reached the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, and laid his robe from him, and covered him with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.
texts.jon.3.7: And he made proclamation and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste anything; let them not feed, nor drink water;
texts.jon.3.8: but let them be covered with sackcloth, both man and beast, and let them cry mightily unto God: yea, let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in his hands.
texts.jon.3.9: Who knoweth whether God will not turn and repent, and turn away from his fierce anger, that we perish not?
texts.jon.3.10: And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil which he said he would do unto them; and he did it not.
texts.jon.4.1: But it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was angry.
texts.jon.4.2: And he prayed unto Jehovah, and said, I pray thee, O Jehovah, was not this my saying, when I was yet in my country? Therefore I hasted to flee unto Tarshish; for I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in lovingkindness, and repentest thee of the evil.
texts.jon.4.3: Therefore now, O Jehovah, take, I beseech thee, my life from me; for it is better for me to die than to live.
texts.jon.4.4: And Jehovah said, Doest thou well to be angry?
texts.jon.4.5: Then Jonah went out of the city, and sat on the east side of the city, and there made him a booth, and sat under it in the shade, till he might see what would become of the city.
texts.jon.4.6: And Jehovah God prepared a gourd, and made it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shade over his head, to deliver him from his evil case. So Jonah was exceeding glad because of the gourd.
texts.jon.4.7: But God prepared a worm when the morning rose the next day, and it smote the gourd, that it withered.
texts.jon.4.8: And it came to pass, when the sun arose, that God prepared a sultry east wind; and the sun beat upon the head of Jonah, that he fainted, and requested for himself that he might die, and said, It is better for me to die than to live.
texts.jon.4.9: And God said to Jonah, Doest thou well to be angry for the gourd? And he said, I do well to be angry, even unto death.
texts.jon.4.10: And Jehovah said, Thou hast had regard for the gourd, for which thou hast not labored, neither madest it grow; which came up in a night, and perished in a night:
texts.jon.4.11: and should not I have regard for Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?

texts.jon.1.1: La parole de l'Eternel fut adressée à Jonas, fils d'Amitthaï, en ces mots:
texts.jon.1.2: Lève-toi, va à Ninive, la grande ville, et crie contre elle! car sa méchanceté est montée jusqu'à moi.
texts.jon.1.3: Et Jonas se leva pour s'enfuir à Tarsis, loin de la face de l'Eternel. Il descendit à Japho, et il trouva un navire qui allait à Tarsis; il paya le prix du transport, et s'embarqua pour aller avec les passagers à Tarsis, loin de la face de l'Eternel.
texts.jon.1.4: Mais l'Eternel fit souffler sur la mer un vent impétueux, et il s'éleva sur la mer une grande tempête. Le navire menaçait de faire naufrage.
texts.jon.1.5: Les mariniers eurent peur, ils implorèrent chacun leur dieu, et ils jetèrent dans la mer les objets qui étaient sur le navire, afin de le rendre plus léger. Jonas descendit au fond du navire, se coucha, et s'endormit profondément.
texts.jon.1.6: Le pilote s'approcha de lui, et lui dit: Pourquoi dors-tu? Lève-toi, invoque ton Dieu! peut-être voudra-t-il penser à nous, et nous ne périrons pas.
texts.jon.1.7: Et ils se dirent l'un à l'autre: Venez, et tirons au sort, pour savoir qui nous attire ce malheur. Ils tirèrent au sort, et le sort tomba sur Jonas.
texts.jon.1.8: Alors ils lui dirent: Dis-nous qui nous attire ce malheur. Quelles sont tes affaires, et d'où viens-tu? Quel est ton pays, et de quel peuple es-tu?
texts.jon.1.9: Il leur répondit: Je suis Hébreu, et je crains l'Eternel, le Dieu des cieux, qui a fait la mer et la terre.
texts.jon.1.10: Ces hommes eurent une grande frayeur, et ils lui dirent: Pourquoi as-tu fait cela? Car ces hommes savaient qu'il fuyait loin de la face de l'Eternel, parce qu'il le leur avait déclaré.
texts.jon.1.11: Ils lui dirent: Que te ferons-nous, pour que la mer se calme envers nous? Car la mer était de plus en plus orageuse.
texts.jon.1.12: Il leur répondit: Prenez-moi, et jetez-moi dans la mer, et la mer se calmera envers vous; car je sais que c'est moi qui attire sur vous cette grande tempête.
texts.jon.1.13: Ces hommes ramaient pour gagner la terre, mais ils ne le purent, parce que la mer s'agitait toujours plus contre eux.
texts.jon.1.14: Alors ils invoquèrent l'Eternel, et dirent: O Eternel, ne nous fais pas périr à cause de la vie de cet homme, et ne nous charge pas du sang innocent! Car toi, Eternel, tu fais ce que tu veux.
texts.jon.1.15: Puis ils prirent Jonas, et le jetèrent dans la mer. Et la fureur de la mer s'apaisa.
texts.jon.1.16: Ces hommes furent saisis d'une grande crainte de l'Eternel, et ils offrirent un sacrifice à l'Eternel, et firent des voeux.
texts.jon.1.17: L'Eternel fit venir un grand poisson pour engloutir Jonas, et Jonas fut dans le ventre du poisson trois jours et trois nuits.
texts.jon.2.1: Jonas, dans le ventre du poisson, pria l'Eternel, son Dieu.
texts.jon.2.2: Il dit: Dans ma détresse, j'ai invoqué l'Eternel, Et il m'a exaucé; Du sein du séjour des morts j'ai crié, Et tu as entendu ma voix.
texts.jon.2.3: Tu m'as jeté dans l'abîme, dans le coeur de la mer, Et les courants d'eau m'ont environné; Toutes tes vagues et tous tes flots ont passé sur moi.
texts.jon.2.4: Je disais: Je suis chassé loin de ton regard! Mais je verrai encore ton saint temple.
texts.jon.2.5: Les eaux m'ont couvert jusqu'à m'ôter la vie, L'abîme m'a enveloppé, Les roseaux ont entouré ma tête.
texts.jon.2.6: Je suis descendu jusqu'aux racines des montagnes, Les barres de la terre m'enfermaient pour toujours; Mais tu m'as fait remonter vivant de la fosse, Eternel, mon Dieu!
texts.jon.2.7: Quand mon âme était abattue au dedans de moi, Je me suis souvenu de l'Eternel, Et ma prière est parvenue jusqu'à toi, Dans ton saint temple.
texts.jon.2.8: Ceux qui s'attachent à de vaines idoles Eloignent d'eux la miséricorde.
texts.jon.2.9: Pour moi, je t'offrirai des sacrifices avec un cri d'actions de grâces, J'accomplirai les voeux que j'ai faits: Le salut vient de l'Eternel.
texts.jon.2.10: L'Eternel parla au poisson, et le poisson vomit Jonas sur la terre.
texts.jon.3.1: La parole de l'Eternel fut adressée à Jonas une seconde fois, en ces mots:
texts.jon.3.2: Lève-toi, va à Ninive, la grande ville, et proclames-y la publication que je t'ordonne!
texts.jon.3.3: Et Jonas se leva, et alla à Ninive, selon la parole de l'Eternel. Or Ninive était une très grande ville, de trois jours de marche.
texts.jon.3.4: Jonas fit d'abord dans la ville une journée de marche; il criait et disait: Encore quarante jours, et Ninive est détruite!
texts.jon.3.5: Les gens de Ninive crurent à Dieu, ils publièrent un jeûne, et se revêtirent de sacs, depuis les plus grands jusqu'aux plus petits.
texts.jon.3.6: La chose parvint au roi de Ninive; il se leva de son trône, ôta son manteau, se couvrit d'un sac, et s'assit sur la cendre.
texts.jon.3.7: Et il fit faire dans Ninive cette publication, par ordre du roi et de ses grands; Que les hommes et les bêtes, les boeufs et les brebis, ne goûtent de rien, ne paissent point, et ne boivent point d'eau!
texts.jon.3.8: Que les hommes et les bêtes soient couverts de sacs, qu'ils crient à Dieu avec force, et qu'ils reviennent tous de leur mauvaise voie et des actes de violence dont leurs mains sont coupables!
texts.jon.3.9: Qui sait si Dieu ne reviendra pas et ne se repentira pas, et s'il ne renoncera pas à son ardente colère, en sorte que nous ne périssions point?
texts.jon.3.10: Dieu vit qu'ils agissaient ainsi et qu'ils revenaient de leur mauvaise voie. Alors Dieu se repentit du mal qu'il avait résolu de leur faire, et il ne le fit pas.
texts.jon.4.1: Cela déplut fort à Jonas, et il fut irrité.
texts.jon.4.2: Il implora l'Eternel, et il dit: Ah! Eternel, n'est-ce pas ce que je disais quand j'étais encore dans mon pays? C'est ce que je voulais prévenir en fuyant à Tarsis. Car je savais que tu es un Dieu compatissant et miséricordieux, lent à la colère et riche en bonté, et qui te repens du mal.
texts.jon.4.3: Maintenant, Eternel, prends-moi donc la vie, car la mort m'est préférable à la vie.
texts.jon.4.4: L'Eternel répondit: Fais-tu bien de t'irriter?
texts.jon.4.5: Et Jonas sortit de la ville, et s'assit à l'orient de la ville, Là il se fit une cabane, et s'y tint à l'ombre, jusqu'à ce qu'il vît ce qui arriverait dans la ville.
texts.jon.4.6: L'Eternel Dieu fit croître un ricin, qui s'éleva au-dessus de Jonas, pour donner de l'ombre sur sa tête et pour lui ôter son irritation. Jonas éprouva une grande joie à cause de ce ricin.
texts.jon.4.7: Mais le lendemain, à l'aurore, Dieu fit venir un ver qui piqua le ricin, et le ricin sécha.
texts.jon.4.8: Au lever du soleil, Dieu fit souffler un vent chaud d'orient, et le soleil frappa la tête de Jonas, au point qu'il tomba en défaillance. Il demanda la mort, et dit: La mort m'est préférable à la vie.
texts.jon.4.9: Dieu dit à Jonas: Fais-tu bien de t'irriter à cause du ricin? Il répondit: Je fais bien de m'irriter jusqu'à la mort.
texts.jon.4.10: Et l'Eternel dit: Tu as pitié du ricin qui ne t'a coûté aucune peine et que tu n'as pas fait croître, qui est né dans une nuit et qui a péri dans une nuit.
texts.jon.4.11: Et moi, je n'aurais pas pitié de Ninive, la grande ville, dans laquelle se trouvent plus de cent vingt mille hommes qui ne savent pas distinguer leur droite de leur gauche, et des animaux en grand nombre!

texts.jon.1.1: Es geschah das Wort des HERRN zu Jona, dem Sohn Amitthais, und sprach:
texts.jon.1.2: Mache dich auf und gehe in die große Stadt Ninive und predige wider sie! denn ihre Bosheit ist heraufgekommen vor mich.
texts.jon.1.3: Aber Jona machte sich auf und floh vor dem HERRN und wollte gen Tharsis und kam hinab gen Japho. Und da er ein Schiff fand, das gen Tharsis wollte fahren, gab er Fährgeld und trat hinein, daß er mit ihnen gen Tharsis führe vor dem HERRN.
texts.jon.1.4: Da ließ der HERR einen großen Wind aufs Meer kommen, und es erhob sich ein großes Ungewitter auf dem Meer, daß man meinte, das Schiff würde zerbrechen.
texts.jon.1.5: Und die Schiffsleute fürchteten sich und schrieen, ein jeglicher zu seinem Gott, und warfen das Gerät, das im Schiff war, ins Meer, daß es leichter würde. Aber Jona war hinunter in das Schiff gestiegen, lag und schlief.
texts.jon.1.6: Da trat zu ihm der Schiffsherr und sprach zu ihm: Was schläfst du? Stehe auf, rufe deinen Gott an! ob vielleicht Gott an uns gedenken wollte, daß wir nicht verdürben.
texts.jon.1.7: Und einer sprach zum andern: Kommt, wir wollen losen, daß wir erfahren, um welches willen es uns so übel gehe. Und da sie losten traf's Jona.
texts.jon.1.8: Da sprachen sie zu ihm: Sage uns, warum geht es uns so übel? was ist dein Gewerbe, und wo kommst du her? Aus welchem Lande bist du, und von welchem Volk bist du?
texts.jon.1.9: Er sprach zu ihnen: Ich bin ein Hebräer und fürchte den HERRN, den Gott des Himmels, welcher gemacht hat das Meer und das Trockene.
texts.jon.1.10: Da fürchteten sich die Leute sehr und sprachen zu ihm: Warum hast du denn solches getan? denn sie wußten, daß er vor dem HERRN floh; denn er hatte es ihnen gesagt.
texts.jon.1.11: Da sprachen sie zu ihm: Was sollen wir denn mit dir tun, daß uns das Meer still werde? Denn das Meer fuhr ungestüm.
texts.jon.1.12: Er sprach zu ihnen: Nehmt mich und werft mich ins Meer, so wird euch das Meer still werden. Denn ich weiß, daß solch groß Ungewitter über euch kommt um meinetwillen.
texts.jon.1.13: Und die Leute trieben, daß sie wieder zu Lande kämen; aber sie konnten nicht, denn das Meer fuhr ungestüm wider sie.
texts.jon.1.14: Da riefen sie zu dem HERRN und sprachen: Ach HERR, laß uns nicht verderben um dieses Mannes Seele willen und rechne uns nicht zu unschuldig Blut! denn du, HERR, tust, wie dir's gefällt.
texts.jon.1.15: Und sie nahmen Jona und warfen ihn ins Meer; das stand das Meer still von seinem Wüten.
texts.jon.1.16: Und die Leute fürchteten den HERR sehr und taten dem HERRN Opfer und Gelübde.
texts.jon.1.17: Aber der HERR verschaffte einen großen Fisch, Jona zu verschlingen. Und Jona war im Leibe des Fisches drei Tage und drei Nächte.
texts.jon.2.1: Und Jona betete zu dem HERRN, seinem Gott, im Leibe des Fisches.
texts.jon.2.2: Und sprach: Ich rief zu dem HERRN in meiner Angst, und er antwortete mir; ich schrie aus dem Bauche der Hölle, und du hörtest meine Stimme.
texts.jon.2.3: Du warfest mich in die Tiefe mitten im Meer, daß die Fluten mich umgaben; alle deine Wogen und Wellen gingen über mich,
texts.jon.2.4: daß ich gedachte, ich wäre von deinen Augen verstoßen, ich würde deinen heiligen Tempel nicht mehr sehen.
texts.jon.2.5: Wasser umgaben mich bis an mein Leben, die Tiefe umringte mich; Schilf bedeckte mein Haupt.
texts.jon.2.6: Ich sank hinunter zu der Berge Gründen, die Erde hatte mich verriegelt ewiglich; aber du hast mein Leben aus dem Verderben geführt, HERR, mein Gott.
texts.jon.2.7: Da meine Seele bei mir verzagte, gedachte ich an den HERRN; und mein Gebet kam zu dir in deinen heiligen Tempel.
texts.jon.2.8: Die da halten an dem Nichtigen, verlassen ihre Gnade.
texts.jon.2.9: Ich aber will mit Dank dir opfern, mein Gelübde will ich bezahlen; denn die Hilfe ist des HERRN.
texts.jon.2.10: Und der HERR sprach zum Fisch, und der spie Jona aus ans Land.
texts.jon.3.1: Und es geschah das Wort des HERRN zum andernmal zu Jona und sprach:
texts.jon.3.2: Mache dich auf, gehe in die große Stadt Ninive und predige ihr die Predigt, die ich dir sage!
texts.jon.3.3: Da machte sich Jona auf und ging hin gen Ninive, wie der HERR gesagt hatte. Ninive aber war eine große Stadt vor Gott, drei Tagereisen groß.
texts.jon.3.4: Und da Jona anfing hineinzugehen eine Tagereise in die Stadt, predigte er und sprach: Es sind noch vierzig Tage, so wird Ninive untergehen.
texts.jon.3.5: Da glaubten die Leute zu Ninive an Gott und ließen predigen, man sollte fasten, und zogen Säcke an, beide, groß und klein.
texts.jon.3.6: Und da das vor den König zu Ninive kam, stand er auf von seinem Thron und legte seinen Purpur ab und hüllte einen Sack um sich und setzte sich in die Asche
texts.jon.3.7: und ließ ausrufen und sagen zu Ninive nach Befehl des Königs und seiner Gewaltigen also: Es sollen weder Mensch noch Vieh, weder Ochsen noch Schafe Nahrung nehmen, und man soll sie nicht weiden noch sie Wasser trinken lassen;
texts.jon.3.8: und sollen Säcke um sich hüllen, beide, Menschen und Vieh, und zu Gott rufen heftig; und ein jeglicher bekehre sich von seinem bösen Wege und vom Frevel seiner Hände.
texts.jon.3.9: Wer weiß? Es möchte Gott wiederum gereuen und er sich wenden von seinem grimmigen Zorn, daß wir nicht verderben.
texts.jon.3.10: Da aber Gott sah ihre Werke, daß sie sich bekehrten von ihrem bösen Wege, reute ihn des Übels, das er geredet hatte ihnen zu tun, und tat's nicht.
texts.jon.4.1: Das verdroß Jona gar sehr, und er ward zornig
texts.jon.4.2: und betete zum HERRN und sprach: Ach HERR, das ist's, was ich sagte, da ich noch in meinem Lande war; darum ich auch wollte zuvorkommen, zu fliehen gen Tharsis; denn ich weiß, daß du gnädig, barmherzig, langmütig und von großer Güte bist und läßt dich des Übels reuen.
texts.jon.4.3: So nimm doch nun, HERR, meine Seele von mir; denn ich wollte lieber tot sein als leben.
texts.jon.4.4: Aber der HERR sprach: Meinst du, daß du billig zürnst?
texts.jon.4.5: Und Jona ging zur Stadt hinaus und setzte sich morgenwärts von der Stadt und machte sich daselbst eine Hütte; darunter setzte er sich in den Schatten, bis er sähe, was der Stadt widerfahren würde.
texts.jon.4.6: Gott der HERR aber verschaffte einen Rizinus, der wuchs über Jona, daß er Schatten gäbe über sein Haupt und errettete ihn von seinem Übel; und Jona freute sich sehr über den Rizinus.
texts.jon.4.7: Aber Gott verschaffte einen Wurm des Morgens, da die Morgenröte anbrach; der stach den Rizinus, daß er verdorrte.
texts.jon.4.8: Als aber die Sonne aufgegangen war, verschaffte Gott einen dürren Ostwind; und die Sonne stach Jona auf den Kopf, daß er matt ward. Da wünschte er seiner Seele den Tod und sprach: Ich wollte lieber tot sein als leben.
texts.jon.4.9: Da sprach Gott zu Jona: Meinst du, daß du billig zürnst um den Rizinus? Und er sprach: Billig zürne ich bis an den Tod.
texts.jon.4.10: Und der HERR sprach: Dich jammert des Rizinus, daran du nicht gearbeitet hast, hast ihn auch nicht aufgezogen, welcher in einer Nacht ward und in einer Nacht verdarb;
texts.jon.4.11: und mich sollte nicht jammern Ninives, solcher großen Stadt, in welcher sind mehr denn hundert und zwanzigtausend Menschen, die nicht wissen Unterschied, was rechts oder links ist, dazu auch viele Tiere?

texts.jon.1.1: И было слово Господне к Ионе, сыну Амафиину:
texts.jon.1.2: встань, иди в Ниневию, город великий, и проповедуй в нем, ибо злодеяния его дошли до Меня.
texts.jon.1.3: И встал Иона, чтобы бежать в Фарсис от лица Господня, и пришел в Иоппию, и нашел корабль, отправлявшийся в Фарсис, отдал плату за провоз и вошел в него, чтобы плыть с ними в Фарсис от лица Господа.
texts.jon.1.4: Но Господь воздвиг на море крепкий ветер, и сделалась на море великая буря, и корабль готов был разбиться.
texts.jon.1.5: И устрашились корабельщики, и взывали каждый к своему богу, и стали бросать в море кладь с корабля, чтобы облегчить его от нее; Иона же спустился во внутренность корабля, лег и крепко заснул.
texts.jon.1.6: И пришел к нему начальник корабля и сказал ему: что ты спишь? встань, воззови к Богу твоему; может быть, Бог вспомнит о нас и мы не погибнем.
texts.jon.1.7: И сказали друг другу: пойдем, бросим жребии, чтобы узнать, за кого постигает нас эта беда. И бросили жребии, и пал жребий на Иону.
texts.jon.1.8: Тогда сказали ему: скажи нам, за кого постигла нас эта беда? какое твое занятие, и откуда идешь ты? где твоя страна, и из какого ты народа?
texts.jon.1.9: И он сказал им: я Еврей, чту Господа Бога небес, сотворившего море и сушу.
texts.jon.1.10: И устрашились люди страхом великим и сказали ему: для чего ты это сделал? Ибо узнали эти люди, что он бежит от лица Господня, как он сам объявил им.
texts.jon.1.11: И сказали ему: что сделать нам с тобою, чтобы море утихло для нас? Ибо море не переставало волноваться.
texts.jon.1.12: Тогда он сказал им: возьмите меня и бросьте меня в море, и море утихнет для вас, ибо я знаю, что ради меня постигла вас эта великая буря.
texts.jon.1.13: Но эти люди начали усиленно грести, чтобы пристать к земле, но не могли, потому что море все продолжало бушевать против них.
texts.jon.1.14: Тогда воззвали они к Господу и сказали: молим Тебя, Господи, да не погибнем за душу человека сего, и да не вменишь нам кровь невинную; ибо Ты, Господи, соделал, что угодно Тебе!
texts.jon.1.15: И взяли Иону и бросили его в море, и утихло море от ярости своей.
texts.jon.1.16: И устрашились эти люди Господа великим страхом, и принесли Господу жертву, и дали обеты.
texts.jon.2.1: И повелел Господь большому киту поглотить Иону; и был Иона во чреве этого кита три дня и три ночи.
texts.jon.2.2: И помолился Иона Господу Богу своему из чрева кита
texts.jon.2.3: и сказал: к Господу воззвал я в скорби моей, и Он услышал меня; из чрева преисподней я возопил, и Ты услышал голос мой.
texts.jon.2.4: Ты вверг меня в глубину, в сердце моря, и потоки окружили меня, все воды Твои и волны Твои проходили надо мною.
texts.jon.2.5: И я сказал: отринут я от очей Твоих, однако я опять увижу святый храм Твой.
texts.jon.2.6: Объяли меня воды до души моей, бездна заключила меня; морскою травою обвита была голова моя.
texts.jon.2.7: До основания гор я нисшел, земля своими запорами навек заградила меня; но Ты, Господи Боже мой, изведешь душу мою из ада.
texts.jon.2.8: Когда изнемогла во мне душа моя, я вспомнил о Господе, и молитва моя дошла до Тебя, до храма святаго Твоего.
texts.jon.2.9: Чтущие суетных и ложных богов оставили Милосердаго своего,
texts.jon.2.10: а я гласом хвалы принесу Тебе жертву; что обещал, исполню: у Господа спасение!
texts.jon.2.11: И сказал Господь киту, и он изверг Иону на сушу.
texts.jon.3.1: И было слово Господне к Ионе вторично:
texts.jon.3.2: встань, иди в Ниневию, город великий, и проповедуй в ней, что Я повелел тебе.
texts.jon.3.3: И встал Иона и пошел в Ниневию, по слову Господню; Ниневия же была город великий у Бога, на три дня ходьбы.
texts.jon.3.4: И начал Иона ходить по городу, сколько можно пройти в один день, и проповедывал, говоря: еще сорок дней и Ниневия будет разрушена!
texts.jon.3.5: И поверили Ниневитяне Богу, и объявили пост, и оделись во вретища, от большого из них до малого.
texts.jon.3.6: Это слово дошло до царя Ниневии, и он встал с престола своего, и снял с себя царское облачение свое, и оделся во вретище, и сел на пепле,
texts.jon.3.7: и повелел провозгласить и сказать в Ниневии от имени царя и вельмож его: "чтобы ни люди, ни скот, ни волы, ни овцы ничего не ели, не ходили на пастбище и воды не пили,
texts.jon.3.8: и чтобы покрыты были вретищем люди и скот и крепко вопияли к Богу, и чтобы каждый обратился от злого пути своего и от насилия рук своих.
texts.jon.3.9: Кто знает, может быть, еще Бог умилосердится и отвратит от нас пылающий гнев Свой, и мы не погибнем".
texts.jon.3.10: И увидел Бог дела их, что они обратились от злого пути своего, и пожалел Бог о бедствии, о котором сказал, что наведет на них, и не навел.
texts.jon.4.1: Иона сильно огорчился этим и был раздражен.
texts.jon.4.2: И молился он Господу и сказал: о, Господи! не это ли говорил я, когда еще был в стране моей? Потому я и побежал в Фарсис, ибо знал, что Ты Бог благий и милосердый, долготерпеливый и многомилостивый и сожалеешь о бедствии.
texts.jon.4.3: И ныне, Господи, возьми душу мою от меня, ибо лучше мне умереть, нежели жить.
texts.jon.4.4: И сказал Господь: неужели это огорчило тебя так сильно?
texts.jon.4.5: И вышел Иона из города, и сел с восточной стороны у города, и сделал себе там кущу, и сел под нею в тени, чтобы увидеть, что будет с городом.
texts.jon.4.6: И произрастил Господь Бог растение, и оно поднялось над Ионою, чтобы над головою его была тень и чтобы избавить его от огорчения его; Иона весьма обрадовался этому растению.
texts.jon.4.7: И устроил Бог так, что на другой день при появлении зари червь подточил растение, и оно засохло.
texts.jon.4.8: Когда же взошло солнце, навел Бог знойный восточный ветер, и солнце стало палить голову Ионы, так что он изнемог и просил себе смерти, и сказал: лучше мне умереть, нежели жить.
texts.jon.4.9: И сказал Бог Ионе: неужели так сильно огорчился ты за растение? Он сказал: очень огорчился, даже до смерти.
texts.jon.4.10: Тогда сказал Господь: ты сожалеешь о растении, над которым ты не трудился и которого не растил, которое в одну ночь выросло и в одну же ночь и пропало:
texts.jon.4.11: Мне ли не пожалеть Ниневии, города великого, в котором более ста двадцати тысяч человек, не умеющих отличить правой руки от левой, и множество скота?

texts.jon.1.1: E veiu a palavra do Senhor a Jonas, filho de Amittai, dizendo:
texts.jon.1.2: Levanta-te, vae á grande cidade de Ninive, e apregoa contra ella, porque a sua malicia subiu até mim.
texts.jon.1.3: E Jonas se levantou para fugir de diante da face do Senhor para Tarsis, e desceu a Joppe, e achou que um navio ia para Tarsis, e deu a sua passagem, e desceu para dentro d’elle, para ir com elles para Tarsis, de diante da face do Senhor.
texts.jon.1.4: Mas o Senhor lançou ao mar um grande vento, e fez-se no mar uma grande tempestade, e o navio estava para quebrar-se.
texts.jon.1.5: Então temeram os marinheiros, e clamavam cada um ao seu deus, e lançavam no mar as fazendas, que estavam no navio, para o alliviarem do seu pezo; porém Jonas desceu aos lados do porão, e se deitou, e dormia um profundo somno.
texts.jon.1.6: E o mestre do navio chegou-se a elle, e disse-lhe: Que tens, adormentado? levanta-te, clama ao teu Deus; porventura Deus se lembrará de nós para que não pereçamos.
texts.jon.1.7: E diziam cada um ao seu companheiro: Vinde, e lancemos sortes, para que saibamos por que causa nos tem vindo este mal. E lançaram sortes, e a sorte caiu sobre Jonas.
texts.jon.1.8: Então lhe disseram: Declara-nos tu agora, por cuja causa nos tem vindo este mal. Que occupação é a tua? e d’onde vens? qual é a tua terra? e de que povo és tu?
texts.jon.1.9: E elle lhes disse: Eu sou hebreo, e temo ao Senhor, o Deus do céu, que fez o mar e a terra secca.
texts.jon.1.10: Então estes homens tremeram com grande temor, e lhe disseram: Porque fizeste tu isto? Pois sabiam os homens que fugia de diante do Senhor, porque elle lh’o tinha declarado.
texts.jon.1.11: E disseram-lhe: Que te faremos nós, para que o mar se nos aquiete? Porque o mar se elevava e engrossava cada vez mais.
texts.jon.1.12: E elle lhes disse: Levantae-me, e lançae-me no mar, e o mar se vos aquietará; porque eu sei que por minha causa é que vos sobreveiu esta grande tempestade.
texts.jon.1.13: Mas os homens remavam, para tornar a trazer o navio para terra, mas não podiam; porquanto o mar se ia embravecendo cada vez mais contra elles.
texts.jon.1.14: Então clamaram ao Senhor, e disseram: Ah Senhor! não pereçamos por causa da alma d’este homem, e não ponhas sobre nós o sangue innocente; porque tu, Senhor, fizeste como quizeste.
texts.jon.1.15: E levantaram a Jonas, e o lançaram no mar, e cessou o mar da sua furia.
texts.jon.1.16: Temeram pois estes homens ao Senhor com grande temor; e sacrificaram sacrificios ao Senhor, e votaram votos.
texts.jon.1.17: Preparou pois o Senhor um grande peixe, que tragasse a Jonas; e esteve Jonas tres dias e tres noites nas entranhas do peixe.
texts.jon.2.1: E orou Jonas ao Senhor, seu Deus, das entranhas do peixe.
texts.jon.2.2: E disse: Da minha angustia clamei ao Senhor, e elle me respondeu; do ventre do inferno gritei, e tu ouviste a minha voz.
texts.jon.2.3: Porque tu me lançaste no profundo, no coração dos mares, e a corrente me tem cercado; todas as tuas ondas e as tuas vagas teem passado por cima de mim.
texts.jon.2.4: E eu dizia: Lançado estou de diante dos teus olhos; todavia tornarei a ver o templo da tua sanctidade.
texts.jon.2.5: As aguas me cercaram até á alma, o abysmo me rodeou, e a alga se embrulhava á minha cabeça.
texts.jon.2.6: Eu desci até aos fundamentos dos montes: os ferrolhos da terra me encerrariam para sempre; mas tu fizeste subir a minha vida da perdição, ó Senhor meu Deus.
texts.jon.2.7: Desfallecendo em mim a minha alma, me lembrei do Senhor; e entrou a ti a minha oração, no templo da tua sanctidade.
texts.jon.2.8: Os que observam as vaidades vãs deixam a sua propria misericordia.
texts.jon.2.9: Mas eu te sacrificarei com a voz do agradecimento; o que votei pagarei: do Senhor vem a salvação.
texts.jon.2.10: Fallou pois o Senhor ao peixe: e vomitou a Jonas na terra.
texts.jon.3.1: E veiu a palavra do Senhor segunda vez a Jonas, dizendo:
texts.jon.3.2: Levanta-te, e vae á grande cidade de Ninive, e prega contra ella a prégação que eu te digo.
texts.jon.3.3: E levantou-se Jonas, e foi a Ninive, segundo a palavra do Senhor: era pois Ninive uma grande cidade de Deus, de tres dias de caminho.
texts.jon.3.4: E começava Jonas a entrar pela cidade caminho d’um dia, e prégava, e dizia: Ainda quarenta dias, e Ninive será subvertida.
texts.jon.3.5: E os homens de Ninive creram em Deus; e proclamaram um jejum, e vestiram-se de sacco, desde o maior até ao menor.
texts.jon.3.6: Porque esta palavra chegou ao rei de Ninive, e levantou-se do seu throno, e tirou de si os seus vestidos, e cobriu-se de sacco, e assentou-se sobre a cinza.
texts.jon.3.7: E fez apregoar, e fallou-se em Ninive, pelo mandado do rei e dos seus grandes, dizendo: Nem homens, nem animaes, nem bois, nem ovelhas provem coisa alguma, nem se lhes dê pasto, nem bebam agua.
texts.jon.3.8: Mas os homens e os animaes estarão cobertos de saccos, e clamarão fortemente a Deus, e se converterão, cada um do seu mau caminho, e da violencia que ha nas suas mãos.
texts.jon.3.9: Quem sabe se se voltará Deus, e se arrependerá, e se apartará do furor da sua ira, de sorte que não pereçamos?
texts.jon.3.10: E Deus viu as obras d’elles, como se converteram do seu mau caminho: e Deus se arrependeu do mal que tinha dito lhes faria, e não o fez.
texts.jon.4.1: E desagradou-se Jonas extremamente d’isso, e ficou todo apaixonado.
texts.jon.4.2: E orou ao Senhor, e disse: Ah! Senhor! não foi esta a minha palavra, estando eu ainda na minha terra? por isto é que me preveni, fugindo para Tarsis, pois sabia que és Deus piedoso, e misericordioso, longanimo e grande em benignidade, e que te arrependes do mal.
texts.jon.4.3: Peço-te, pois, ó Senhor, tira-me a minha alma, porque melhor me é morrer do que viver.
texts.jon.4.4: E disse o Senhor: É bem feito que assim te apaixones?
texts.jon.4.5: Jonas, pois, saiu da cidade, e assentou-se ao oriente da cidade: e ali fez uma cabana, e se assentou debaixo d’ella, á sombra, até ver que era o que acontecia á cidade.
texts.jon.4.6: E preparou o Senhor Deus uma aboboreira, e a fez subir por cima de Jonas, para que fizesse sombra sobre a sua cabeça, a fim de o livrar do seu enfado: e Jonas se alegrou com grande alegria por causa da aboboreira.
texts.jon.4.7: Mas Deus enviou um bicho, no dia seguinte ao subir da alva, e feriu a aboboreira, e se seccou.
texts.jon.4.8: E aconteceu que, apparecendo o sol, Deus ordenou um vento calmoso oriental, e o sol feriu a cabeça de Jonas; e elle desmaiou, e desejou com toda a sua alma morrer, dizendo: Melhor me é morrer do que viver.
texts.jon.4.9: Então disse Deus a Jonas: É bem feito que assim te apaixones por causa da aboboreira? E elle disse: É bem feito que me apaixone até á morte.
texts.jon.4.10: E disse o Senhor: Tiveste tu compaixão da aboboreira, na qual não trabalhaste, nem a fizeste crescer, que n’uma noite nasceu, e n’uma noite pereceu;
texts.jon.4.11: E não hei de eu ter compaixão da grande cidade de Ninive em que estão mais de cento e vinte mil homens que não sabem discernir entre a sua mão direita e a sua mão esquerda, e muitos animaes?

texts.jon.1.1: Now the word of the LORD came to Jonah the son of Amittai, saying,
texts.jon.1.2: Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me.
texts.jon.1.3: But Jonah arose to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the LORD, and went down to Joppa; and he found a ship going to Tarshish: so he paid the fare of it, and went down into it, to go with them to Tarshish from the presence of the LORD.
texts.jon.1.4: But the LORD sent out a great wind into the sea, and there was a mighty tempest in the sea, so that the ship was in danger of being broken.
texts.jon.1.5: Then the mariners were afraid, and cried every man to his god, and cast the wares that were in the ship into the sea, to lighten it of them. But Jonah had gone down into the sides of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.
texts.jon.1.6: So the ship-master came to him, and said to him, What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God, it may be that God will think upon us, that we perish not.
texts.jon.1.7: And they said every one to his fellow, Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil is upon us. So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.
texts.jon.1.8: Then said they to him, Tell us, we pray thee, for whose cause this evil is upon us; What is thy occupation? and whence comest thou? what is thy country? and of what people art thou?
texts.jon.1.9: And he said to them, I am a Hebrew; and I fear the LORD, the God of heaven, who hath made the sea and the dry land.
texts.jon.1.10: Then were the men exceedingly afraid, and said to him, Why hast thou done this? For the men knew that he fled from the presence of the LORD, because he had told them.
texts.jon.1.11: Then said they to him, What shall we do to thee, that the sea may be calm to us? for the sea wrought, and was tempestuous.
texts.jon.1.12: And he said to them, Take me, and cast me into the sea; so shall the sea be calm to you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you.
texts.jon.1.13: Nevertheless the men rowed hard to bring it to the land; but they could not: for the sea wrought, and was tempestuous against them.
texts.jon.1.14: Wherefore they cried to the LORD, and said, We beseech thee, O LORD, we beseech thee, let us not perish for this man's life, and lay not upon us innocent blood: for thou, O LORD, hast done as it pleased thee.
texts.jon.1.15: So they took Jonah, and cast him into the sea: and the sea ceased from her raging.
texts.jon.1.16: Then the men feared the LORD exceedingly, and offered a sacrifice to the LORD, and made vows.
texts.jon.1.17: Now the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
texts.jon.2.1: Then Jonah prayed to the LORD his God out of the fish's belly,
texts.jon.2.2: And said, I cried by reason of my affliction to the LORD, and he heard me; out of the belly of hell cried I, and thou heardst my voice.
texts.jon.2.3: For thou hadst cast me into the deep, in the midst of the seas; and the floods encompassed me: all thy billows and thy waves passed over me.
texts.jon.2.4: Then I said, I am cast out of thy sight; yet I will look again towards thy holy temple.
texts.jon.2.5: The waters encompassed me, even to the soul: the depth inclosed me on every side, the weeds were wrapped about my head.
texts.jon.2.6: I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with her bars was about me for ever: yet hast thou brought up my life from corruption, O LORD my God.
texts.jon.2.7: When my soul fainted within me I remembered the LORD: and my prayer came to thee, into thy holy temple.
texts.jon.2.8: They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy.
texts.jon.2.9: But I will sacrifice to thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that which I have vowed. Salvation is of the LORD.
texts.jon.2.10: And the LORD spoke to the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.
texts.jon.3.1: And the word of the LORD came to Jonah the second time, saying,
texts.jon.3.2: Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and preach to it the preaching that I bid thee.
texts.jon.3.3: So Jonah arose, and went to Nineveh, according to the word of the LORD. Now Nineveh was an exceeding great city of three days' journey.
texts.jon.3.4: And Jonah began to enter into the city a day's journey, and he cried, and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.
texts.jon.3.5: So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.
texts.jon.3.6: For word came to the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, and he laid his robe from him, and covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.
texts.jon.3.7: And he caused it to be proclaimed and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed, nor drink water:
texts.jon.3.8: But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily to God: yes, let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands.
texts.jon.3.9: Who can tell if God will turn and repent, and turn away from his fierce anger, that we perish not?
texts.jon.3.10: And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do to them; and he did it not.
texts.jon.4.1: But it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was very angry.
texts.jon.4.2: And he prayed to the LORD, and said, I pray thee, O LORD was not this my saying, when I was yet in my country? Therefore I fled before to Tarshish: for I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repentest of the evil.
texts.jon.4.3: Therefore now, O LORD, take, I beseech thee, my life from me; for it is better for me to die than to live.
texts.jon.4.4: Then said the LORD, Doest thou well to be angry?
texts.jon.4.5: So Jonah went out of the city, and sat on the east side of the city, and there made him a booth, and sat under it in the shade, till he might see what would become of the city.
texts.jon.4.6: And the LORD God prepared a gourd, and made it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shade over his head, to deliver him from his grief. So Jonah was exceeding glad of the gourd.
texts.jon.4.7: But God prepared a worm when the morning rose the next day, and it smote the gourd that it withered.
texts.jon.4.8: And it came to pass, when the sun rose that God prepared a vehement east wind; and the sun beat upon the head of Jonah, that he fainted, and wished in himself to die, and said, It is better for me to die than to live.
texts.jon.4.9: And God said to Jonah, Doest thou well to be angry for the gourd? And he said, I do well to be angry, even to death.
texts.jon.4.10: Then said the LORD, Thou hast had pity on the gourd, for which thou hast not labored, neither made it grow; which came up in a night, and perished in a night:
texts.jon.4.11: And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, in which are more than a hundred and twenty thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand, and also many cattle?

texts.jon.1.1: And the word of Jehovah came unto Jonah the son of Amittai, saying,
texts.jon.1.2: Arise, go to Nineveh, the great city, and cry against it; for their wickedness is come up before me.
texts.jon.1.3: But Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of Jehovah; and he went down to Joppa, and found a ship going to Tarshish; so he paid the fare thereof, and went down into it, to go with them unto Tarshish, from the presence of Jehovah.
texts.jon.1.4: But Jehovah sent out a great wind upon the sea, and there was a mighty tempest upon the sea, so that the ship was like to be broken.
texts.jon.1.5: And the mariners were afraid, and cried every one unto his god; and they cast forth the wares that were in the ship into the sea, to be lightened of them. But Jonah had gone down into the lower part of the ship; and he lay, and was fast asleep.
texts.jon.1.6: And the shipmaster came to him, and said unto him, What meanest thou, sleeper? arise, call upon thy God; perhaps God will think upon us, that we perish not.
texts.jon.1.7: And they said each one to his fellow, Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know for whose cause this evil is upon us. And they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.
texts.jon.1.8: And they said unto him, Tell us, we pray thee, for whose cause this evil is upon us: what is thine occupation? and whence comest thou? what is thy country? and of what people art thou?
texts.jon.1.9: And he said unto them, I am a Hebrew, and I fear Jehovah, the God of the heavens, who hath made the sea and the dry [land].
texts.jon.1.10: Then were the men exceedingly afraid, and said unto him, What is this thou hast done? For the men knew that he fled from the presence of Jehovah: for he had told them.
texts.jon.1.11: And they said unto him, What shall we do unto thee, that the sea may be calm unto us? for the sea grew more and more tempestuous.
texts.jon.1.12: And he said unto them, Take me up, and cast me forth into the sea; so shall the sea be calm unto you: for I know that because of me this great tempest is upon you.
texts.jon.1.13: But the men rowed hard to regain the land; but they could not; for the sea grew more and more tempestuous against them.
texts.jon.1.14: And they cried unto Jehovah and said, Ah, Jehovah, we beseech thee, let us not perish for this man's life, and lay not upon us innocent blood: for thou, Jehovah, hast done as it pleased thee.
texts.jon.1.15: And they took up Jonah, and cast him forth into the sea: and the sea ceased from its raging.
texts.jon.1.16: And the men feared Jehovah exceedingly, and offered a sacrifice unto Jehovah, and made vows.
texts.jon.1.17: And Jehovah prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
texts.jon.2.1: And Jonah prayed unto Jehovah his God out of the fish's belly;
texts.jon.2.2: and he said: I cried by reason of my distress unto Jehovah, and he answered me; Out of the belly of Sheol cried I: thou heardest my voice.
texts.jon.2.3: For thou didst cast me into the depth, into the heart of the seas, And the flood was round about me: All thy breakers and thy billows are gone over me.
texts.jon.2.4: And I said, I am cast out from before thine eyes, Yet will I look again toward thy holy temple.
texts.jon.2.5: The waters encompassed me, to the soul: The deep was round about me, The weeds were wrapped about my head.
texts.jon.2.6: I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; The bars of the earth [closed] upon me for ever: But thou hast brought up my life from the pit, O Jehovah my God.
texts.jon.2.7: When my soul fainted within me, I remembered Jehovah; And my prayer came in unto thee, Into thy holy temple.
texts.jon.2.8: They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy.
texts.jon.2.9: But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that which I have vowed. Salvation is of Jehovah.
texts.jon.2.10: And Jehovah commanded the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry [land].
texts.jon.3.1: And the word of Jehovah came unto Jonah the second time, saying,
texts.jon.3.2: Arise, go to Nineveh, the great city, and preach unto it the preaching that I shall bid thee.
texts.jon.3.3: And Jonah arose, and went unto Nineveh, according to the word of Jehovah. Now Nineveh was an exceeding great city of three days' journey.
texts.jon.3.4: And Jonah began to enter into the city a day's journey, and he cried and said, Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!
texts.jon.3.5: And the men of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them.
texts.jon.3.6: And the word reached the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, and laid his robe from him, and covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.
texts.jon.3.7: And he caused it to be proclaimed and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste anything: let them not feed, nor drink water;
texts.jon.3.8: and let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily unto God; and let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands.
texts.jon.3.9: Who knoweth but that God will turn and repent, and will turn away from his fierce anger, that we perish not?
texts.jon.3.10: And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil that he had said he would do unto them, and he did [it] not.
texts.jon.4.1: And it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was angry.
texts.jon.4.2: And he prayed unto Jehovah, and said, Ah, Jehovah, was not this my saying when I was yet in my country? Therefore I was minded to flee at first unto Tarshish; for I knew that thou art a gracious ùGod, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great loving-kindness, and repentest thee of the evil.
texts.jon.4.3: And now, Jehovah, take, I beseech thee, my life from me, for it is better for me to die than to live.
texts.jon.4.4: And Jehovah said, Doest thou well to be angry?
texts.jon.4.5: And Jonah went out of the city, and sat on the east side of the city, and there made him a booth, and sat under it in the shade, till he might see what would become of the city.
texts.jon.4.6: And Jehovah Elohim prepared a gourd, and made it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shade over his head, to deliver him from his trouble. And Jonah was exceeding glad because of the gourd.
texts.jon.4.7: But God prepared a worm when the morning rose the next day, and it smote the gourd, that it withered.
texts.jon.4.8: And it came to pass, when the sun arose, that God prepared a sultry east wind; and the sun beat upon the head of Jonah, so that he fainted; and he requested for himself that he might die, and said, It is better for me to die than to live.
texts.jon.4.9: And God said to Jonah, Doest thou well to be angry for the gourd? And he said, I do well to be angry, unto death.
texts.jon.4.10: And Jehovah said, Thou hast pity on the gourd, for which thou hast not laboured, neither madest it grow; which came up in a night, and perished in a night:
texts.jon.4.11: and I, should not I have pity on Nineveh, the great city, wherein are more than a hundred and twenty thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?

texts.jon.1.1: And there is a word of Jehovah unto Jonah son of Amittai, saying:
texts.jon.1.2: `Rise, go unto Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim against it that their wickedness hath come up before Me.'
texts.jon.1.3: And Jonah riseth to flee to Tarshish from the face of Jehovah, and goeth down [to] Joppa, and findeth a ship going [to] Tarshish, and he giveth its fare, and goeth down into it, to go with them to Tarshish from the face of Jehovah.
texts.jon.1.4: And Jehovah hath cast a great wind on the sea, and there is a great tempest in the sea, and the ship hath reckoned to be broken;
texts.jon.1.5: and the mariners are afraid, and cry each unto his god, and cast the goods that [are] in the ship into the sea, to make [it] light of them; and Jonah hath gone down unto the sides of the vessel, and he lieth down, and is fast asleep.
texts.jon.1.6: And the chief of the company draweth near to him, and saith to him, `What -- to thee, O sleeper? rise, call unto thy God, it may be God doth bethink himself of us, and we do not perish.'
texts.jon.1.7: And they say each unto his neighbour, `Come, and we cast lots, and we know on whose account this evil [is] on us.' And they cast lots, and the lot falleth on Jonah.
texts.jon.1.8: And they say unto him, `Declare to us, we pray thee, on what account this evil [is] on us? what [is] thine occupation, and whence comest thou? what [is] thy country, seeing thou art not of this people?'
texts.jon.1.9: And he saith unto them, `A Hebrew I [am], and Jehovah, God of the heavens, I am reverencing, who made the sea and the dry land.'
texts.jon.1.10: And the men fear a great fear, and say unto him, `What [is] this thou hast done!' for the men have known that from the face of Jehovah he is fleeing, for he hath told them.
texts.jon.1.11: And they say unto him, `What do we do to thee that the sea may cease from us, for the sea is more and more tempestuous?'
texts.jon.1.12: And he saith unto them, `Lift me up, and cast me into the sea, and the sea doth cease from you; for I know that on my account this great tempest [is] upon you.'
texts.jon.1.13: And the men row to turn back unto the dry land, and are not able, for the sea is more and more tempestuous against them.
texts.jon.1.14: And they cry unto Jehovah, and say, `We pray Thee, O Jehovah, let us not, we pray Thee, perish for this man's life, and do not lay on us innocent blood, for Thou, Jehovah, as Thou hast pleased, Thou hast done.'
texts.jon.1.15: And they lift up Jonah, and cast him into the sea, and the sea ceaseth from its raging;
texts.jon.1.16: and the men fear Jehovah -- a great fear, and sacrifice a sacrifice to Jehovah, and vow vows.
texts.jon.1.17: And Jehovah appointeth a great fish to swallow up Jonah, and Jonah is in the bowels of the fish three days and three nights.
texts.jon.2.1: And Jonah prayeth unto Jehovah his God from the bowels of the fish.
texts.jon.2.2: And he saith: I called, because of my distress, to Jehovah, And He doth answer me, From the belly of sheol I have cried, Thou hast heard my voice.
texts.jon.2.3: When Thou dost cast me [into] the deep, Into the heart of the seas, Then the flood doth compass me, All Thy breakers and Thy billows have passed over me.
texts.jon.2.4: And I -- I said: I have been cast out from before Thine eyes, (Yet I add to look unto Thy holy temple!)
texts.jon.2.5: Compassed me have waters unto the soul, The deep doth compass me, The weed is bound to my head.
texts.jon.2.6: To the cuttings of mountains I have come down, The earth, her bars [are] behind me to the age. And Thou bringest up from the pit my life, O Jehovah my God.
texts.jon.2.7: In the feebleness within me of my soul Jehovah I have remembered, And come in unto Thee doth my prayer, Unto Thy holy temple.
texts.jon.2.8: Those observing lying vanities their own mercy forsake.
texts.jon.2.9: And I -- with a voice of thanksgiving -- I sacrifice to Thee, That which I have vowed I complete, Salvation [is] of Jehovah.
texts.jon.2.10: And Jehovah saith to the fish, and it vomiteth out Jonah on the dry land.
texts.jon.3.1: And there is a word of Jehovah unto Jonah a second time, saying,
texts.jon.3.2: `Rise, go unto Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim unto it the proclamation that I am speaking unto thee;'
texts.jon.3.3: and Jonah riseth, and he goeth unto Nineveh, according to the word of Jehovah. And Nineveh hath been a great city before God, a journey of three days.
texts.jon.3.4: And Jonah beginneth to go in to the city a journey of one day, and proclaimeth, and saith, `Yet forty days -- and Nineveh is overturned.'
texts.jon.3.5: And the men of Nineveh believe in God, and proclaim a fast, and put on sackcloth, from their greatest even unto their least,
texts.jon.3.6: seeing the word doth come unto the king of Nineveh, and he riseth from his throne, and removeth his honourable robe from off him, and spreadeth out sackcloth, and sitteth on the ashes,
texts.jon.3.7: and he crieth and saith in Nineveh by a decree of the king and his great ones, saying, `Man and beast, herd and flock -- let them not taste anything, let them not feed, even water let them not drink;
texts.jon.3.8: and cover themselves [with] sackcloth let man and beast, and let them call unto God mightily, and let them turn back each from his evil way, and from the violence that [is] in their hands.
texts.jon.3.9: Who knoweth? He doth turn back, and God hath repented, and hath turned back from the heat of His anger, and we do not perish.'
texts.jon.3.10: And God seeth their works, that they have turned back from their evil way, and God repenteth of the evil that He spake of doing to them, and he hath not done [it].
texts.jon.4.1: And it is grievous unto Jonah -- a great evil -- and he is displeased at it;
texts.jon.4.2: and he prayeth unto Jehovah, and he saith, `I pray Thee, O Jehovah, is not this my word while I was in mine own land -- therefore I was beforehand to flee to Tarshish -- that I have known that Thou [art] a God, gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in kindness, and repenting of evil?
texts.jon.4.3: And now, O Jehovah, take, I pray Thee, my soul from me, for better [is] my death than my life.'
texts.jon.4.4: And Jehovah saith, `Is doing good displeasing to thee?'
texts.jon.4.5: And Jonah goeth forth from the city, and sitteth on the east of the city, and maketh to himself there a booth, and sitteth under it in the shade, till that he seeth what is in the city.
texts.jon.4.6: And Jehovah God appointeth a gourd, and causeth it to come up over Jonah, to be a shade over his head, to give deliverance to him from his affliction, and Jonah rejoiceth because of the gourd [with] great joy.
texts.jon.4.7: And God appointeth a worm at the going up of the dawn on the morrow, and it smiteth the gourd, and it drieth up.
texts.jon.4.8: And it cometh to pass, about the rising of the sun, that God appointeth a cutting east wind, and the sun smiteth on the head of Jonah, and he wrappeth himself up, and asketh his soul to die, and saith, `Better [is] my death than my life.'
texts.jon.4.9: And God saith unto Jonah: `Is doing good displeasing to thee, because of the gourd?' and he saith, `To do good is displeasing to me -- unto death.'
texts.jon.4.10: And Jehovah saith, `Thou hast had pity on the gourd, for which thou didst not labour, neither didst thou nourish it, which a son of a night was, and a son of a night perished,
texts.jon.4.11: and I -- have not I pity on Nineveh, the great city, in which there are more than twelve myriads of human beings, who have not known between their right hand and their left -- and much cattle!'

texts.jon.1.1: Y fue palabra de Jehová a Jonás, hijo de Amati, diciendo:
texts.jon.1.2: Levántate, y vé a Nínive, ciudad grande, y pregona contra ella; porque su maldad ha subido delante de mí.
texts.jon.1.3: Y Jonás se levantó para huir de la presencia de Jehová a Társis, y descendió a Joppe; y halló un navío que se partía para Társis, y pagándole su pasaje entró en él para irse con ellos a Társis, de delante de Jehová.
texts.jon.1.4: Mas Jehová hizo levantar un gran viento en la mar, e hízose una gran tempestad en la mar, que la nao pensó ser quebrada.
texts.jon.1.5: Y los marineros tuvieron temor, y cada uno llamaba a su dios; y echaron a la mar el cargamento que llevaban en la nao, para descargarla de ello. Jonás empero se había descendido a los costados de la nao, y se había echado a dormir.
texts.jon.1.6: Y el maestre de la nao se llegó a él, y le dijo: ¿Qué tienes dormilón? Levántate, y clama a tu dios, quizá él habrá compasión de nosotros, y no pereceremos.
texts.jon.1.7: Y dijeron cada uno a su compañero: Veníd, y echemos suertes, para saber por quien nos ha venido este mal. Y echaron suertes, y la suerte cayó sobre Jonás.
texts.jon.1.8: Y ellos le dijeron: Decláranos ahora, ¿por qué nos ha venido este mal? ¿Qué oficio tienes, y de donde vienes, cual es tu tierra, y de qué pueblo eres?
texts.jon.1.9: Y él les respondió: Hebreo soy, y a Jehová Dios de los cielos temo, que hizo la mar y la tierra.
texts.jon.1.10: Y aquellos hombres temieron de gran temor, y le dijeron: ¿Por qué hiciste esto? Porque ellos entendieron que huía de delante de Jehová; porque él se lo había declarado.
texts.jon.1.11: Y dijéronle: ¿Qué te haremos, para que la mar se nos quiete? porque la mar iba, y se embravecía.
texts.jon.1.12: El les respondió: Tomádme, y echádme a la mar, y la mar se os quietará; porque yo sé que por mí ha venido sobre vosotros esta grande tempestad.
texts.jon.1.13: Y aquellos hombres trabajaron por tornar la nao a tierra, mas no pudieron; porque la mar iba y se embravecía sobre ellos.
texts.jon.1.14: Y clamaron a Jehová, y dijeron: Rogámoste ahora, Jehová, que no perezcamos nosotros por la vida de aqueste hombre, ni pongas sobre nosotros sangre inocente; porque tú, Jehová, has hecho como has querido.
texts.jon.1.15: Y tomaron a Jonás, y echáronle a la mar; y la mar se quietó de su ira.
texts.jon.1.16: Y temieron aquellos hombres a Jehová con gran temor; y ofrecieron sacrificio a Jehová, y prometieron votos.
texts.jon.1.17: Mas Jehová había aparejado un gran pez, que tragase a Jonás; y estuvo Jonás en el vientre del pez tres días y tres noches.
texts.jon.2.1: Y oró Jonás desde el vientre del pez a Jehová su Dios,
texts.jon.2.2: Y dijo: Clamé de mi tribulación a Jehová, y él me oyó: del vientre del infierno clamé, y oíste mi voz.
texts.jon.2.3: Echásteme en el profundo, en medio de las mares, y la corriente me rodeó: todas tus ondas y tus olas pasaron sobre mí.
texts.jon.2.4: Y yo dije: Echado soy de delante de tus ojos, mas aun veré el templo santo tuyo.
texts.jon.2.5: Las aguas me rodearon hasta el alma, el abismo me rodeó, el junco se enguedejó a mi cabeza.
texts.jon.2.6: Descendí a las raíces de los montes: la tierra echó sus cerraduras sobre mí para siempre: mas tú sacaste mi vida de la sepultura, o! Jehová Dios mío.
texts.jon.2.7: Cuando mi alma desfallecía en mí, me acordé de Jehová; y mi oración entró hasta ti en tu santo templo.
texts.jon.2.8: Los que guardan las vanidades vanas, su misericordia desamparan.
texts.jon.2.9: Yo empero con voz de alabanza te sacrificaré: pagaré lo que prometí: a Jehová sea el salvamento.
texts.jon.2.10: Y mandó Jehová al pez, y vomitó a Jonás en tierra.
texts.jon.3.1: Y fue palabra de Jehová segunda vez a Jonás, diciendo:
texts.jon.3.2: Levántate, y vé a Nínive aquella gran ciudad, y pregona en ella el pregón que yo te diré.
texts.jon.3.3: Y levantóse Jonás, y fue a Nínive, conforme a la palabra de Jehová. Y Nínive era ciudad grande en gran manera, de tres días de camino.
texts.jon.3.4: Y comenzó Jonás a entrar por la ciudad camino de un día, y pregonaba, diciendo: De aquí a cuarenta días Nínive será destruida.
texts.jon.3.5: Y los varones de Nínive creyeron a Dios; y pregonaron ayuno, y vistiéronse de sacos, desde el mayor de ellos hasta el menor de ellos.
texts.jon.3.6: Y llegó el negocio hasta el rey de Nínive, y levantóse de su trono, y echó de sí su vestido, y cubrióse de saco, y asentóse sobre ceniza.
texts.jon.3.7: E hizo pregonar, y decir: En Nínive, por mandado del rey, y de sus grandes, diciendo: Hombres y animales, bueyes y ovejas, no gusten cosa, ni se les dé pasto, ni beban agua.
texts.jon.3.8: Y los hombres, y los animales se cubran de sacos, y clamen a Dios fuertemente; y cada uno se convierta de su mal camino, de la rapiña que está en sus manos.
texts.jon.3.9: ¿Quién sabe si se convertirá, y se arrepentirá Dios; y se convertirá del furor de su ira, y no pereceremos?
texts.jon.3.10: Y vio Dios lo que hicieron, porque se convirtieron de su mal camino; y arrepintióse del mal que había dicho que les había de hacer, y no lo hizo.
texts.jon.4.1: Y a Jonás le pesó de gran pesar, y se enojó.
texts.jon.4.2: Y oró a Jehová, y dijo: Ahora, Jehová, ¿no es esto lo que yo decía estando en mi tierra, por lo cual previne huyéndome a Társis? Porque yo sabía que tú eres Dios clemente y piadoso, tardo a enojarte, y de grande misericordia, y que te arrepientes del mal.
texts.jon.4.3: Ahora pues, Jehová, ruégote que me mates; porque mejor me es la muerte que la vida.
texts.jon.4.4: Y Jehová le dijo: ¿Haces tú bien de enojarte tanto?
texts.jon.4.5: Y salióse Jonás de la ciudad, y asentó hacia el oriente de la ciudad; e hízose allí una choza, y asentóse debajo de ella a la sombra, hasta ver que sería de la ciudad.
texts.jon.4.6: Y preparó Jehová Dios una calabacera, la cual creció sobre Jonás, para que hiciese sombra sobre su cabeza, y le defendiese de su mal; y Jonás se alegró grandemente por la calabacera.
texts.jon.4.7: Y el mismo Dios preparó un gusano en viniendo la mañana del día siguiente, el cual hirió a la calabacera, y se secó.
texts.jon.4.8: Y acaeció que en saliendo el sol preparó Dios un viento solano grande; y el sol hirió a Jonás en la cabeza, y desmayábase; y pedía a su alma la muerte, diciendo: Mejor sería para mí la muerte que mi vida.
texts.jon.4.9: Entonces dijo Dios a Jonás: ¿Tanto te enojas por la calabacera? Y él respondió: Mucho me enojo, hasta desear la muerte.
texts.jon.4.10: Y dijo Jehová: ¿Tuviste tú piedad de la calabacera en la cual no trabajaste, ni tú la hiciste crecer, que en espacio de una noche nació, y en espacio de otra noche pereció:
texts.jon.4.11: Y no tendré yo piedad de Nínive aquella grande ciudad, donde hay más de ciento y veinte mil hombres, que no conocen su mano derecha ni su mano izquierda, y muchos animales?

texts.jon.1.1: And the word of Yahweh came unto Jonah son of Amittai, saying:
texts.jon.1.2: Arise, get thee to Nineveh the great city, and proclaim unto it,—that their wickedness, hath come up, before me.
texts.jon.1.3: But Jonah arose to flee unto Tarshish, away from the presence of Yahweh,—and went down to Joppa, and found a ship going to Tarshish, so he paid the fare thereof, and went down into it, to go with them to Tarshish, away from the presence of Yahweh.
texts.jon.1.4: But, Yahweh, hurled a great wind against the sea,—and, there arose a mighty tempest in the sea,—and, the ship, thought to be broken in pieces,
texts.jon.1.5: Then were the mariners, afraid, and made outcry every man unto his own god, and they hurled the wares which were in the ship, into the sea, to lighten it of them,—but, Jonah, had gone down into the hinder parts of the vessel, and had lain down, and fallen into a sound sleep.
texts.jon.1.6: Then drew near unto him the shipmaster, and said to him, What meanest thou, O sound sleeper? Arise, cry unto thy God, Peradventure God will bethink himself of us, that we perish not.
texts.jon.1.7: And they said—every one unto his fellow, Come, and let us cast lots, that we may get to know for whose sake this calamity is upon us. So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.
texts.jon.1.8: Then said they unto him, Tell us, we pray thee, for whose sake this calamity is upon us? What is thy business? and from whence comest thou? what is thy country? and of what people art thou?
texts.jon.1.9: And he said unto them, A Hebrew, am I,—and, Yahweh, the God of the heavens, do, I, revere, him who made the sea, and the dry land.
texts.jon.1.10: Then did the men revere with great reverence, and said unto him, What is it thou hast done? For the men knew that, away from the presence of Yahweh, he was fleeing,—for he had told them.
texts.jon.1.11: Then said they unto him, What shall we de to thee, that the sea may cease raging over us? For, the sea, was raging more and more.
texts.jon.1.12: And he said unto them, Take me up, and hurl me into the sea, that the sea may cease raging over you,—for I do know that, for my sake, is this great tempest upon you.
texts.jon.1.13: Nevertheless the men, wrought hard, to bring it back unto the land, but could not,—for, the sea, was raging over them more and more.
texts.jon.1.14: Then cried they unto Yahweh, and said, Ah now, Yahweh, pray let it not be that we perish for this man’s life, neither lay upon us innocent blood,—for, thou, O Yahweh, as thou hast pleased, hast ever done.
texts.jon.1.15: So they took up Jonah and hurled him into the sea,—and the sea, left off, her roaring.
texts.jon.1.16: Then did the men revere Yahweh with a great reverence,—and offered sacrifice to Yahweh, and vowed vows.
texts.jon.1.17: Now Yahweh had appointed a great fish, to swallow up Jonah,—and Jonah was in the belly of the fish, three days and three nights.
texts.jon.2.1: Then prayed Jonah, unto Yahweh, his God,—out of the belly of the fish;
texts.jon.2.2: and said—I cried—out of my distress—unto Yahweh, and he answered me,—Out of the belly of hades, called I, Thou didst hear my voice.
texts.jon.2.3: For thou hast cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and, a flood, enveloped me,—All thy breakers and thy rolling waves, over me, passed.
texts.jon.2.4: And, I, said, I am driven out from before thine eyes,—Yet will I again have regard unto thy holy temple:
texts.jon.2.5: The waters, encompassed me, to the peril of my life, The roaring deep, enveloped me,—The sea-weed, was wrapped about my head:
texts.jon.2.6: To the roots of the mountains, went I down, As for the earth, her bars, were about me, age-abidingly,—Then didst thou bring up—out of the pit—my life, O Yahweh my God.
texts.jon.2.7: When my soul, darkened itself over me, Yahweh, I remembered,—and my prayer, came in unto thee, unto thy holy temple.
texts.jon.2.8: They who take heed to the vanities of falsehood, do, their own lovingkindness, forsake.
texts.jon.2.9: But, I, with the voice of praise, will sacrifice unto thee, What I have vowed, I will pay,—Salvation, belongeth to Yahweh!
texts.jon.2.10: So then Yahweh spake unto the fish,—and it vomited out Jonah, upon the dry land.
texts.jon.3.1: Then came the word of Yahweh unto Jonah, the second time, saying:
texts.jon.3.2: Arise, get thee unto Nineveh, the great city,—and cry against it the cry that I am bidding thee.
texts.jon.3.3: So Jonah arose, and went his way unto Nineveh, according to the word of Yahweh,—Nineveh, being a city great before God, of three days’ journey.
texts.jon.3.4: So Jonah began to enter into the city, one day’s journey,—and he cried out and said—Yet forty days, and, Nineveh, is to be overthrown!
texts.jon.3.5: And the people of Nineveh believed in God,—and proclaimed a fast, and clothed themselves in sackcloth, from the greatest of them, even unto the least of them.
texts.jon.3.6: And the word reached unto the king of Nineveh, so he arose from his throne, and laid aside his robe from off him,—and covered him with sackcloth, and sat on ashes.
texts.jon.3.7: And he caused an outcry to be made—and said—throughout Nineveh, By decree of the king and of his great men, Be it known:—Man and beast, herd and flock, Let them taste, nothing, let them not feed, and, water, let them not drink:
texts.jon.3.8: Let both man and beast, cover themselves with sackcloth, and let them cry unto God, mightily,—Yea let them turn, every man from his wicked way, and from the violence which is in their hands:
texts.jon.3.9: Who knoweth whether God himself—may turn and grieve,—and turn away from the glow of his anger, that we perish not?
texts.jon.3.10: And God saw their doings, that they turned from their wicked way,—and God was grieved over the calamity which he had spoken of executing upon them, and executed it not.
texts.jon.4.1: And it was vexing unto Jonah, with a great vexation,—and it angered him.
texts.jon.4.2: So he prayed unto Yahweh, and said—Ah now! Yahweh! Was not, this, my word, while I was yet upon mine own soil? For this cause, did I hasten to flee unto Tarshish,—because I knew that, thou, art a GOD of favour and compassion, slow to anger, and abundant in lovingkindness, and art grieved over calamity.
texts.jon.4.3: Now, therefore, O Yahweh, take, I pray thee, my life from me,—for it were better for me, to die, than, to live.
texts.jon.4.4: Then said Yahweh, Art thou rightly angry?
texts.jon.4.5: But Jonah, went forth, out of the city, and abode on the east side of the city; and made for himself there, a hut, and sat under it, in the shade, until he should see what would become of the city.
texts.jon.4.6: Now Yahweh God appointed a gourd, and caused it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shade over his head, to deliver him from his vexation,—and Jonah rejoiced over the gourd, with great rejoicing.
texts.jon.4.7: But God appointed a worm, at the uprisings of the dawn, the next day,—and it smote the gourd, that it withered.
texts.jon.4.8: And it came to pass, at the breaking forth of the sun, that God appointed a sultry east wind, and the sun smote upon the head of Jonah, that he became faint,—and asked his life, that he might die, and said, It were better for me, to die, than, to live.
texts.jon.4.9: Then said God unto Jonah, Art thou rightly angry over the gourd? And he said, I am rightly angry, unto death.
texts.jon.4.10: Then said Yahweh, Thou, wouldest have spared the gourd, for which thou hadst not toiled, neither hadst thou made it grow,—which, as the off-spring of a night, came up, and, as the offspring of a night, perished;
texts.jon.4.11: And was not, I, to spare Nineveh, the great city,—wherein are more than twelve times ten thousand human beings, who cannot discern between their right hand and their left, besides much cattle?

texts.jon.1.1: La palabra de Yahvé llegó a Jonás, hijo de Amitai, diciendo:
texts.jon.1.2: «Levántate, ve a Nínive, esa gran ciudad, y predica contra ella, porque su maldad ha subido hasta mi presencia».
texts.jon.1.3: Pero Jonás se levantó para huir a Tarsis, lejos de la presencia de Yahvé. Bajó a Jope y encontró una nave que iba a Tarsis; pagó el pasaje y embarcó para ir con ellos a Tarsis, lejos de la presencia de Yahvé.
texts.jon.1.4: Pero Yahvé envió un fuerte viento sobre el mar, y se desató una tempestad tan poderosa que la nave corría el riesgo de romperse.
texts.jon.1.5: Entonces los marineros tuvieron miedo y cada uno clamó a su dios. Arrojaron al mar la carga que había en la nave para aligerarla. Pero Jonás había bajado al interior de la nave y se había acostado, y estaba profundamente dormido.
texts.jon.1.6: El patrón de la nave se le acercó y le dijo: «¿Qué haces ahí dormido? ¡Levántate, invoca a tu Dios! Tal vez tu Dios se fije en nosotros, para que no perezcamos».
